## The finding `crime_00064` — **Duplicate Component Shape** (medium, confidence 0.70), detector `duplicate_component_shape.js`, shape hash `e96b55b64336…`, 4 occurrences across 4 files: | File | Lines | |---|---| | `dashboard/final-example/app/ui/invoices/create-form.tsx` | 142–150 | | `dashboard/final-example/app/ui/invoices/edit-form.tsx` | 152–160 | | `dashboard/starter-example/app/ui/invoices/create-form.tsx` | 101–109 | | `dashboard/starter-example/app/ui/invoices/edit-form.tsx` | 112–120 | Reading the four sites, the repeated subtree is the **form footer**, and it is byte-identical in all four except the submit label: ```tsx
Cancel {/* or "Edit Invoice" */}
``` Exactly one axis varies: `"Create Invoice"` vs `"Edit Invoice"`. Everything else — the cancel destination, the eight utility classes on the `Link`, the gap/justify layout — is copied. That's the drift surface: a hover-state change, an `h-10` bump, or an accessibility fix (the `Link` has no `role`/focus ring distinct from the button) has to land in four places, and the `starter-example` copies will silently fall behind because nobody edits the starter when fixing the final. ## Scope decision first `final-example` and `starter-example` are two independent Next.js apps (separate `app/`, separate `@/` alias roots) — the same tutorial at two stages. **Extract per app, twice; do not build a cross-app shared package.** Sharing across them would couple the "before" and "after" states of a teaching fixture and give the starter code it isn't supposed to have yet. That drops each app from 2 copies to 1, which is the whole available win here. ## Proposed shared component `FormActions` — the submit/cancel footer for a dashboard form. **New files (one per app):** - `dashboard/final-example/app/ui/form-actions.tsx` - `dashboard/starter-example/app/ui/form-actions.tsx` Placed at `app/ui/` rather than `app/ui/invoices/` because the shape is form-generic, not invoice-specific — `login-form.tsx` is the obvious next adopter. ### Public API ```tsx import Link from 'next/link'; import { Button } from '@/app/ui/button'; import type { ReactNode } from 'react'; export function FormActions({ submitLabel, cancelHref, cancelLabel = 'Cancel', pending = false, children, }: { /** Text on the submit button — the only thing every call site must supply. */ submitLabel: string; /** Where Cancel navigates. Required: silently defaulting to the invoices * list is how a customers form ends up cancelling to the wrong page. */ cancelHref: string; cancelLabel?: string; /** Disables submit while a server action is in flight. */ pending?: boolean; /** Slot: extra actions rendered left of Cancel (e.g. a destructive Delete). */ children?: ReactNode; }) { return (
{children} {cancelLabel}
); } ``` **Props:** `submitLabel` (required), `cancelHref` (required), `cancelLabel` (optional, defaults `'Cancel'`), `pending` (optional). **Slots:** one — `children`, rendered before Cancel, for the destructive/tertiary action that an invoice edit form will eventually want. Deliberately a single slot: separate `leading`/`trailing` render props would be API surface with no current caller. `cancelHref` is required on purpose. All four current call sites pass the same value, so a default would be free today — but the default is a landmine the moment this is reused on a customers or settings form, and that is precisely the kind of copy-forward mistake this detector exists to catch. `pending` and `children` are additive-but-unused at extraction time. If you'd rather ship strictly what's needed, drop both and keep `{ submitLabel, cancelHref, cancelLabel? }` — adding them later is non-breaking. ### Call sites after the change ```tsx // final-example/app/ui/invoices/create-form.tsx (replaces lines 142–150) // final-example/app/ui/invoices/edit-form.tsx (replaces lines 152–160) ``` …and the identical pair in `starter-example` at lines 101–109 and 112–120. ## Files that change **Modified (4)** — delete the footer `
`, add `import { FormActions } from '@/app/ui/form-actions';`, drop the now-unused `Link` and `Button` imports **only if** nothing else in the file uses them (in all four files they're used solely by this footer, so both imports go): - `dashboard/final-example/app/ui/invoices/create-form.tsx` (imports L4, L11; body L142–150) - `dashboard/final-example/app/ui/invoices/edit-form.tsx` (imports L10, L11; body L152–160) - `dashboard/starter-example/app/ui/invoices/create-form.tsx` (body L101–109) - `dashboard/starter-example/app/ui/invoices/edit-form.tsx` (body L112–120) **Added (2):** the two `app/ui/form-actions.tsx` files above. `FormActions` renders no hooks, so it needs no `'use client'` of its own — it inherits the boundary from the four callers, which are already `'use client'`. ## Risk and verification Low. Pure JSX relocation, no behaviour change, no state touched — matching the finding's `effort: small` and `risk: medium` on the `extract_shared_component` action. Two things to confirm rather than assume: 1. **`Button`'s import path differs by app** — verify `@/app/ui/button` resolves in `starter-example` before copying the file across; the alias roots are separate. 2. **Re-run `crimes scan --format json`** and confirm hash `e96b55b64336…` no longer appears. Four call sites collapsing to two `FormActions` invocations should clear it entirely. ## What this does *not* fix Two adjacent findings share these files and are **not** addressed by `FormActions` — worth naming so they don't get assumed away: - `crime_00064` covers only the footer. The much larger duplication in these files — the whole customer-select / amount-input / status-fieldset body, ~120 near-identical lines between each create/edit pair — isn't in this finding. It's the bigger win and a separate, riskier extraction (`defaultValue` threading, `defaultChecked` on the radios). - `crime_00065` / `crime_00066` (`"pending"` / `"paid"` compared across 4 files in 2 expression shapes) live in the status fieldset, not the footer. They need the policy-function fix, independently.
